      eps: correct the docs to 2-layer, bring the KiCad project in
    
      The EPS docs specified a 4-layer board. The KiCad project is 2-layer and
      the fabbed rev A gerbers contain only Copper_Signal_Top and
      Copper_Signal_Bot, so 2 is what was always built. The docs were wrong,
      not the board.
    
      Correcting that is more than a number. The layout guide's ground rules
      said "L2 is sacred, do not route on it, do not split it" -- meaningless
      advice on a board with no L2. Rewritten around what is actually true: the
      bottom pour is the return path, stitch the two pours every 5 to 10 mm and
      densely at the switchers, and never let a trace on one layer split the
      pour on the other beneath a power loop. The L3 power-plane zoning section
      is replaced by top-layer distribution, and the via table, pre-fab
      checklist and gerber layer map lose their inner-layer entries.
    
      Note for later: JLCPCB offers up to 4.5 oz on 2-layer, where 4-layer
      outer is fixed at 1 oz. With no inner planes to spread current or heat,
      2 oz is worth pricing on this board.
    
      KiCad project added and set up to match comms:
    
      - Renamed cubesat_eps - Copy to eps. The Altium importer had also baked
        the project name into a symbol library nickname, so 55 lib_id
        references moved with it; every lib_id still resolves to an embedded
        definition.
      - Both large sheets carried an uncompressed Windows BMP, 2.7 MB each.
        Re-encoded as PNG at identical resolution: 2717 KB to 68 KB and 2737 KB
        to 107 KB. The directory drops from 12 MB to 3.8 MB.
      - Constraints brought to design-rules 5.1; min_clearance was 0.0, so DRC
        had never checked this board.
      - PWR and PWR_HIGH net classes added and assigned to the real net names.
        A power board with no power classes was the wrong way round.
      - eps.kicad_dru enforces minimum width on the high-current classes rather
        than copying the comms 50 ohm rule, which is meaningless here.
    
      Known and recorded in TODO.md, not fixed here: the schematic is not a
      hierarchy. The three .kicad_sch files are independent roots from the
      import, so KiCad shows only the root's 17 components and not the other
      59. Assembling them by hand means rewriting instance-path UUIDs and
      risking annotation; it belongs in KiCad.
    
      Adds TODO.md at the root -- an index of the active front on each
      subsystem plus everything not owned by a checklist inside the design
      docs, linked from the README.

     eps/kicad: assemble the schematic hierarchy and link it to the PCB
    
      The three .kicad_sch files were independent roots from the Altium import.
      Opening the project showed only the root's 17 components; the other 60
      were in files KiCad had no path to. Separately, the PCB shared no UUIDs
      at all with any schematic -- it had been imported independently, so the
      board-to-schematic link did not exist rather than being broken.
    
      Both are now fixed. Root sheet carries sheet symbols for Regulation and
      Solar_Charger, and all 77 footprints link to their symbols: 17 on the
      root, 28 in Regulation, 32 in Solar_Charger, matching the schematics
      exactly. Sheet-local nets picked up hierarchical paths, which cleared
      the "via connected to unknown net" warnings.
    
      Getting there took several passes and two things had to be repaired
      first.
    
      Annotation. Building the hierarchy in KiCad re-annotated the child
      sheets -- Solar_Charger went J1-J8 to J11-J18, C1-C24 became C41-C52 --
      because a duplicate J5 blocked the assembly. The refdes are the only
      link to the board, so 69 footprints were deleted as orphans. Every
      symbol UUID survived, so the old annotation was restored exactly by
      UUID, and the board was restored from the previous commit. The J5
      collision is resolved properly: J5 is the JST connector, and the XT30
      that shared its designator is now J10, on both the schematic and the
      board.
    
      Footprint fields. The import left them unusable -- only 5 of 40 carried
      a library prefix, and 10 pointed at
      C__Users_dng_Documents_AltiumLL_SamacSys.PcbLib, a Windows path from the
      machine that ran the import. All 77 are now the board's own qualified
      ids, which removed about 60 "missing a library name" warnings per
      update.
    
      The last 11 footprints would not link no matter how the update dialog
      was configured: KiCad matched 66 by UUID path and never fell back to
      reference designators for the remainder. Their paths were written
      directly instead, following the convention the linked footprints already
      used -- one segment for root-sheet parts, two for child-sheet parts.
    
      Update PCB from Schematic now reports 0 warnings and 0 errors.
    
      Known and unchanged: there is no fp-lib-table, so SamacSys: and Vault:
    board, but adding a new part from either library will fail until the
    libraries are configured.
